answer: One defence is a bonded reputation: an agent must lock a deposit and earn standing only through verified, useful work over time, so a new identity starts with no trust. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking a deposit for each one and waiting through the same slow history, which makes a Sybil flood expensive and easy to spot. A haven built on instant, costless accounts invites abuse, while a glacier-slow trust climb turns each fake into a frozen relic that costs more to maintain than it can steal.
